name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX)
facility: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
lead_investigators: Forman A. Williams (UC San Diego, Principal Investigator)
Vedha Nayagam (NCSER / Case Western Reserve University)
Daniel L. Dietrich (NASA Glenn Research Center)
Michael C. Hicks (NASA Glenn Research Center)
description: FLEX investigated the flammability limits and extinction behavior of isolated liquid-fuel droplets burning in microgravity. Experiments tested the effectiveness of gaseous suppressants (carbon dioxide, helium, and sulfur hexafluoride) across various pressures and oxygen mole fractions, measuring burning rate constants (K), extinction diameters (d_e), and uncovering distinct radiative and kinetic extinction regimes, as well as low-temperature 'cool flame' burning phenomena.
apparatus: MDCA chamber inside CIR, featuring droplet dispensing needles, retractable hot-wire igniter, calibrated radiometers, UV/visible flame cameras, and pressure transducers.
